title: 23.10 HuMoniX: A 57.3fps 12.8TFLOPS/W Text-to-Motion Processor with Inter-Iteration Output Sparsity and Inter-Frame Joint Similarity
problem: 3D human motion generation via transformer-based diffusion models requires iterative denoising for each motion frame, leading to two bottlenecks: (1) high compute load from diffusion iteration, (2) redundant joint computations across iterations and frames.
motivation: Real-time 3D human motion generation is critical for VR/AR entertainment and media production; accelerating transformer-diffusion inference enables interactive motion synthesis from text prompts.
method: HuMoniX generates 3D motion by iteratively refining noisy predictions into clear motion—a process called diffusion denoising. It exploits two opportunities to reduce computation: pruning denoising computations that barely affect the output across iterations, and reusing joint calculations across frames since joints move gradually between frames. The hardware dataflow and scheduling are specialized to efficiently handle these sparse patterns.
key_novelty: It accelerates text-to-motion generation by identifying and exploiting two forms of redundant computation: denoising steps that barely matter across iterations and joint calculations that repeat across frames.
contributions: Inter-iteration output sparsity pruning identifies and skips negligible denoising steps
Inter-frame joint similarity detection enables shared intermediate computation
Specialized dataflow hardware supporting variable iteration and frame-reuse patterns
Achieves 57.3fps real-time text-to-motion generation with 12.8TFLOPS/W efficiency
limitations: Motion quality metrics (LPIPS, FID), comparison with state-of-the-art motion-generation systems, and energy breakdown not discussed.
primary_theme: Sparsity-exploiting processor for real-time transformer-diffusion text-to-motion synthesis
